title: Some Roman theologians still hold that no work of unbelievers is morally good
source_text: XXXI. Reperiuntur tamen in Schola Romana nonnulli, qui contra quod Bulla citata decernitur, affirmant nullum opus infidelium esse moraliter bonum. Idque quoniam ut opus sit secundum virtutem, & moraliter bonum, non solum fieri debet id quod oportet, sed etiam debet fieri quando, & quantum, & cujus gratia oportet. Finis autem cujus gratia omne opus fieri debet, est Deus ab agente dilectus, in quem reliqua referantur: quia cum Deus solus sit propter se diligendus, omnis affectus qui non fertur in Deum tanquam in finem est malus. Unde concludunt nullum opus infidelium bonum esse, propterea quod veri Dei notitiam non habent, ac proinde nullam suam operationem in verum Deum tanquam in finem ultimum referunt.
pass_a_gloss: XXXI. Yet there are found in the Roman School some, who against what is decreed by the cited Bull, affirm that no work of unbelievers is morally good. And this since for a work to be according to virtue, and morally good, not only must that be done which is fitting, but also it must be done when, and how much, and for whose sake it is fitting. But the end for whose sake every work must be done, is God loved by the agent, to whom the rest are referred: because since God alone is to be loved for his own sake, every affection which is not borne to God as to the end is evil. Whence they conclude that no work of unbelievers is good, because they do not have the knowledge of the true God, and accordingly refer none of their operation to the true God as to the last end.
pass_b_english: Yet some in the Roman School, against what the bull decrees, affirm that no work of unbelievers is morally good. Their reason is that for a work to be virtuous and morally good, it is not enough to do what ought to be done; it must also be done when, as much as, and for the sake for which it ought to be done.

The end for whose sake every work must be done is God, loved by the one acting, and everything else is referred to him. Since God alone is to be loved for his own sake, every affection not directed to God as its end is evil. So they conclude that no work of unbelievers is good, because they do not know the true God and so refer none of their acts to him as last end.

choices.why: One without faith; in XXVIII Estius narrows it to the pagan who lacks knowledge even of the one God, so 'unbeliever' with 'pagan' and 'heathen' where the text specifies.
